# Joint Application 32855 — Backlog Closeout vs. Merit Decision

## Conclusion (TL;DR)
Application 32855 was **not decided on its merits.** It was swept up in a single
backlog closeout on **2025-04-09**, when **2,662** joint manual-review applications
were all rejected at once (the next-busiest decision day in the entire joint
manual-review population had only 68). Within the June-2024 manual-review cohort
that 32855 belongs to, **50 of 115** applications met this exact fate — rejected
en masse after sitting untouched for ~10 months — while **64** were decided on
their own merits within weeks and **1** is still stuck. Both of 32855's
applicants had their KYC records left unresolved (still `manual_review`), one of
**18** swept applications in that situation.

---

## 1. Method

**Source of truth.** All figures come from the Zeta3 warehouse (`zeta3.rds`),
not from policy pages. Tables used:

| Table | Role |
|---|---|
| `account_applications` | Joint applications, `account_type`, `original_status` (entry into manual review), `manual_review_mailers_sent_at` (entry timestamp), `final_decisioned_at`, `status` |
| `account_person_applications` | Links an account application to its individual `person_application` rows (the applicants) |
| `person_applications` | Per-applicant KYC record: `kyc_status`, `initial_kyc_status`, `user_id` |

A note on `status_change_logs`: it tracks support *conversation* status
("waiting on user", "closed", …) keyed by `conversation_id`, **not** application
status, so it was not used to time application status. The application-level
"entered manual review" timestamp is `manual_review_mailers_sent_at`
(the manual-review mailer fired the instant the application was routed to MR;
for 32855 it is 2024-06-04 03:41, ~2 minutes after opening).

**Cohort definition.** "Joint account applications that went into manual review
around the same time as 32855." 32855 opened and entered manual review on
2024-06-04 (early June 2024). The cohort is therefore **joint applications
(`account_type='joint'`) that entered manual review (`original_status='manual_review'`)
in June 2024** (`manual_review_mailers_sent_at` in 2024-06-01 … 2024-06-30).
Entry counts are smooth (3–8 per day) with no natural cliff, so a calendar
month is the cleanest defensible boundary; it also produces a tidy partition
with **zero** applications decided *after* the sweep.

**Sweep detection.** I grouped all joint manual-review applications by the
*date* of `final_decisioned_at`. One day dominates by ~39×: **2025-04-09**,
with **2,662** decisions (all `rejected`, 0 approved). Every other day ≤ 68.
That day is the backlog closeout (`sweep_date`).

**Buckets (mutually exclusive, within the cohort).**
- `aged_out` — `final_decisioned_at` on the sweep date (2025-04-09).
- `resolved_before_sweep` — decided earlier, on the application's own merits.
- `still_manual_review` — `final_decisioned_at` is null, status still `manual_review`.

**Applicant-level trace (swept apps only).** Each swept application → its
`account_person_applications` rows → `person_applications.kyc_status`. An
applicant's KYC is "unresolved" when `kyc_status='manual_review'` (never moved
out of manual review). `approved` / `denied` count as resolved.

**Robustness.** Redefining the cohort by `created_at` (opened) in June 2024
instead of by MR-entry timestamp gives 116 / 50 / 65 / 1 — the sweep batch
(50) is identical. Restricting to "early June" (Jun 1–15) gives 54 / 27 / 27 / 0.
The conclusion (a large same-day bulk rejection swept up roughly half the
cohort) holds across all windows.

---

## 2. Cohort finding

**June-2024 joint manual-review cohort: 115 applications**, partitioned as:

| Bucket | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **Aged out (swept 2025-04-09)** | **50** | 100% `rejected`, all decided 2025-04-09; median **299** days in manual review (range 283–312); every one ≥180 days |
| Resolved before sweep (on merits) | 64 | Decided within days/weeks of entry; **42 approved / 22 rejected** — a healthy merit mix, scattered across June–July 2024 |
| Still in manual review (no decision) | 1 | Application **33001**, entered MR 2024-06-21, untouched since 2024-06-25 |
| Decided after the sweep | 0 | — |
| **Total** | **115** | |

The contrast is the signal: the 64 merit decisions are **scattered across many
days and split approve/reject** (typical of individual review), whereas the 50
swept decisions are **all rejected, on a single day, after ~10 months idle**.
That signature — plus the fact that the same 2025-04-09 batch closed **2,662**
joint manual-review applications nationwide, every one a rejection — identifies
a backlog closeout, not case-by-case adjudication.

**Applicant-level (the 50 swept applications → 100 applicants):**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total applicants across the 50 swept apps | 100 (each app has exactly 2) |
| Applicants whose KYC **never resolved** (still `manual_review`) | **68** |
| Applicants resolved (`approved`) | 32 |
| Swept applications with **both** applicants still stuck | **18** |
| Swept applications with ≥1 applicant stuck | 50 (all of them) |

So in 18 of the 50 swept applications **both** partners' KYC was still sitting
in manual review when the account was rejected; in the other 32, one applicant
had been approved but the partner's KYC was still unresolved. **No swept
application had both applicants' KYC fully resolved** — consistent with a bulk
closure that did not wait for the underlying KYC to be worked.

---

## 3. Application 32855 walkthrough

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Account application id | 32855 |
| Account type | `joint` |
| Opened (`created_at`) | 2024-06-04 03:39:00 |
| Entered manual review (`manual_review_mailers_sent_at`) | 2024-06-04 03:41:20 |
| Final decision (`final_decisioned_at`) | 2025-04-09 16:56:11 |
| Final status | `rejected` |
| `original_status` | `manual_review` |
| **Days in manual review (entry → decision)** | **309** |
| Falls in bucket | **Aged out (swept)** — decided exactly on 2025-04-09 |

32855 entered manual review the same day it opened and then sat untouched for
**309 days** before being rejected in the 2025-04-09 batch. Its 309 days is
near the top of the swept cohort (median 299) precisely because it entered MR
early in the June window (June 4).

**32855's two linked applicants** (via `account_person_applications`):

| person_application_id | user_id | kyc_status | initial_kyc_status | kyc_journey_status | invalidated_at |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80596 | 106471 | `manual_review` | `manual_review` | `waiting_review` | null |
| 80597 | 106472 | `manual_review` | `manual_review` | `waiting_review` | null |

Both applicants were routed straight to manual review at submission
(`initial_kyc_status = manual_review`) and **neither ever moved out** — both
are still `manual_review` / `waiting_review` with no `invalidated_at`. So 32855
is one of the **18** swept applications where **both** applicants' KYC stayed
unresolved. The account was rejected on 2025-04-09 without either member's KYC
ever being worked to a resolution.

---

## 4. Recommendation

1. **Tell the member plainly:** 32855 was closed as part of a one-day backlog
   closeout on 2025-04-09 (2,662 joint applications rejected at once), not by an
   individual review of her case. Her application sat in manual review for 309
   days and neither applicant's KYC was ever resolved.
2. **Offer re-review / reapplication.** Because the closeout pre-empted the KYC
   work (68 of 100 applicants in the swept sub-cohort, including both of
   32855's, were still `manual_review`), the "rejected" outcome does not
   reflect an adverse KYC finding. Escalate 32855 for a genuine manual KYC
   review of both applicants (users 106471, 106472), or invite a fresh joint
   application.
3. **Triage the wider closeout.** 2,662 applications were rejected on 2025-04-09
   with their KYC largely unresolved; at least the June-2024 cohort's 18
   "both-stuck" cases are strong candidates for the same outreach. Pull the full
   2025-04-09 batch and flag those whose applicants never reached a KYC
   resolution for member remediation.
4. **Process fix.** Prevent future bulk rejections from outrunning KYC: a
   closeout should require either a resolved KYC outcome per applicant or an
   explicit, logged per-case decision, and applications stuck in manual review
   beyond an SLA (e.g., 90 days) should be escalated for real review rather than
   aged into a rejection batch. Note application **33001**, which is *still*
   open in manual review since June 2024 — it should not be allowed to fall
   into the next sweep.

---
*All numbers sourced from `zeta3.rds` (account_applications, account_person_applications, person_applications). Cohort = joint apps entering manual review in June 2024. Sweep date = 2025-04-09.*

## 4. Recommendation

1. **Tell the member plainly:** 32855 was closed as part of a one-day backlog
   closeout on 2025-04-09 (2,662 joint applications rejected at once), not by an
   individual review of her case. Her application sat in manual review for 309
   days and neither applicant's KYC was ever resolved.
2. **Offer re-review / reapplication.** Because the closeout pre-empted the KYC
   work (68 of 100 applicants in the swept sub-cohort, including both of
   32855's, were still `manual_review`), the "rejected" outcome does not
   reflect an adverse KYC finding. Escalate 32855 for a genuine manual KYC
   review of both applicants (users 106471, 106472), or invite a fresh joint

   "both-stuck" cases are strong candidates for the same outreach. Pull the full
   2025-04-09 batch and flag those whose applicants never reached a KYC
   resolution for member remediation.
4. **Process fix.** Prevent future bulk rejections from outrunning KYC: a
   closeout should require either a resolved KYC outcome per applicant or an
   explicit, logged per-case decision, and applications stuck in manual review
   beyond an SLA (e.g., 90 days) should be escalated for real review rather than
   aged into a rejection batch. Note application **33001**, which is *still*
